text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- The Bulgarian cabinet said a visiting World Bank mission had offered an aid package of three credits totalling $260 million this year to help the country out of the financial crisis.
-- A court in Bulgaria's second city of Plovdiv sentenced Turkish citizen Kamuran Dogu to 10 years in prison for spying. @
-- Bulgaria's state Bulgargas, Bulgarian firm Gemet and Germany's Zimmermann & Jansen GmbH set up a join stock firm in Sofia for gas production and industrial armature, Bulgargas said.
-- Bulgaria and Romania are expected to hold negotiations in Bucharest today and tomorrow to set up a duty free trade zone, Bulgaria's Trade ministry said.
-- Bulgaria's Construction and regional development ministry said 8,417,683 Bulgarians resident in the country and abroad would be eligible to vote in the parliamentary elections on April 19.
-- More than 50 percent of Bulgarian army officers support Bulgaria's bid to join NATO, a Defence ministry poll showed.

-- Bulgaria's central bank is expected to raise minimum capital requirements for local banks to some 10 billion levs from current 1.4 billion levs and 2.2 billion levs, needed for a domestic and a full banking licence, respectively, the newspaper said without quoting sources.
-- Bulgarians have withdrawn some $42 million deposits from local commercial banks in February as lev-denominated prices of basic goods soared, central bank figures showed. @

-- Bulgaria is negotiating to repay its debts to Poland and Hungary by exports of goods and triangular financial operations, chairman of the Bulgarian Economic Chamber Bozhidar Danev said. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
